title: David's Tomb
visualBrief: Named Mount Zion tomb blocks and attached Upper Room on three complete native plans: irregular stepped pale limestone walls, deep courtyard recesses, flat roof terraces with physical parapets, small recessed window/arched-door openings, the native mapped roof dome and a slender historic roof minaret. Excludes neighboring Dormition Abbey, cemetery, sculpture and interiors.

appearance.colorEncoding: sRGB palette decoded to linear COLOR_0

geographicProposal.groundContactBasis: Three original named building plans and a roof-dome polygon define the signed true-east frame. A fixed open western approach point outside all body plans defines the approximate terrain datum; no roof-return fitting or whole-compound platform.

terrainReference.basis: Open western approach outside the named northern tomb block establishes a fixed approximate ground datum before terrain acquisition. Local foundation and courtyard contact require geographic-preview review.

geographicProposal.notes: Native original polygons control plan, not layer tag integers as literal floor heights.1878exterior controls historic stone/massing typology; modern roof fixtures, exact elevations and minaret attachment remain photographic medium-fi interpretations.

limitations: Complete original named tomb and immediately attached Upper Room plans retain their signed shape and courtyard recesses. Native layer integers are not interpreted as measured elevations. Body heights7.6/9.2/11.2m, dome rise, minaret dimensions/attachment and small façade openings are photographic medium-fi estimates, not a measured architectural survey.

The exact Qualla-published1878Bonfils exterior is the unambiguously public-domain visual control for stone, stepped massing, arches, low dome and slender minaret. Current native plans/roof dome are separate controls. Modern fittings, restored details and the survival of every1878roof item are not asserted; interiors/curtains and unrelated archaeological imagery are excluded.

Exterior assembly only: no Tomb sarcophagus, religious textiles or inscriptions, Upper Room interior, neighboring Dormition Abbey/other monasteries, cemetery, memorial sculpture or landscape reconstruction. No photographic textures or exterior image links embedded in OSM tags were used.

Host terrain/foundation and courtyard contact are approximate. Footings extend0.4m below a fixed western dry-approach datum; source terrain is preserved and no platform/blanket ground opening is introduced.
